The Rolling Stones have sold over 240 million albums worldwide.[434] In 2010, *Rolling Stone* ranked them as fourth on their list of the Greatest Artists of All Time;[435] three years later, *Rolling Stone* declared them the "most definitional band that rock & roll has produced".[422] *The Telegraph* has called Mick Jagger "the Rolling Stone who changed music".[420] The band has been the subject of numerous documentaries and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame by Pete Townshend in 1989.[436][437] The Rolling Stones have inspired and mentored new generations of musical artists both as a band[438][439] and individually.[440][441] They are also credited with changing the "whole business model of popular music".[420] The only artists to top the UK Album Charts in six different decades, they are tied with Elvis Presley and Robbie Williams for the second most number 1 albums on the Official UK Chart, surpassed only by the Beatles.[372]

The Rolling Stones' estimated record sales of 200 million make them one of the best-selling music artists of all time. The band have won three Grammy Awards and a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. Their first stable line-up consisted of vocalist Mick Jagger, guitarist Keith Richards, multi-instrumentalist Brian Jones, bassist Bill Wyman, and drummer Charlie Watts.
